forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

compliance.notes: Strong on the 2021-Code fundamentals: a full-debt-profile liability benchmark charted to 2070/71, reconciled CFR and capital expenditure indicators, a thorough MRP policy with VRP overpayment disclosure, and complete governance/adoption appendices with a named scrutiny committee and quarterly reporting. Weakest on the newer commercial-investment disclosures: the net commercial/service income ratio (PI-08) is cited but never quantified, there is no limit on principal invested beyond 364 days (PI-10), no monetary service/commercial investment limits (COM-09), and formal statements are missing for paras 51-53 compliance, sterling-only borrowing and audit-qualification flagging. Several indicator tables also carry stale year labels (maturity limits headed 2025/26; interest-rate exposures ending 2026/27).

gaps.evidence: s58640 p.3 para 9: the required net commercial/service income to net revenue stream indicator is cited as a Code requirement, but no ratio or figures are produced anywhere
s58640 p.48: non-specified/property-fund investment levels can only be increased with Council approval; no quantified GBP or % ceiling on principal invested beyond 364 days per year
s58640 p.4 para 10: quotes the duty to state compliance with Prudential Code para 51, but no explicit compliance statement referencing paras 51-53 is actually made
s58640 p.48: pooled-fund (property fund) levels capped at approved amounts, increases requiring full Council approval; no stated monetary limits on total service or commercial investment
s58640 p.46: quantified fixed/variable exposure limits for investments only; no portfolio-level risk indicator (e.g. weighted-average credit score or duration)

news_drafts.headline: Hastings forecasts £596k net overspend for 2026/27, to be met from the General Reserve
news_drafts.lead:
Hastings Borough Council forecasts a net overspend of £596,000 for 2026/27, to be funded from the General Reserve after earmarked reserves and other budget adjustments. The September (period 6) monitoring report to Cabinet shows £759k of overspend before earmarked reserves are applied. The paper says a draw on the General Reserve was not expected when the balanced budget was approved.

Housing reports a £390,000 overspend for the year. The 2026/27 budget assumed 350 households would need privately procured temporary accommodation by March 2027; the paper puts the number at 462, with 590 households in temporary accommodation of all kinds at the end of September. It attributes the overspend to demand above the budget assumption, says placement numbers are showing signs of stabilisation, and says a review of the Housing budget and its cost drivers has started.

Cemetery and Crematorium is forecasting a £96.7k overspend from lower-than-expected cremation numbers and reduced income, which the paper links to a national decline in deaths and the growth of direct cremation providers. Salary slippage in the Street Cleansing direct services organisation partly offsets it, leaving Environment and Operations £78.4k over. The Chief Legal Officer and Monitoring Officer's area forecasts a £252.9k overspend, attributed to higher legal costs, increased caseloads and agency staff covering vacancies, alongside temporary transition costs of a new shared service with Lewes District Council.

news_drafts.headline: Hastings Council reschedules £11m debt for £2.3m lifetime savings
news_drafts.lead: Hastings Council has identified £2.3 million in lifetime savings by refinancing six loans worth £11 million, the Full Council heard on Wednesday. The council will take advantage of early repayment discounts worth £5 million to reduce replacement funding to less than £6 million, generating annual savings of around £515,000 in the first two years. The Treasury Management Update reported an additional £2.9 million net present value benefit from the restructuring. The move is part of efforts to strengthen financial resilience ahead of Local Government Reorganisation in April 2028. The council's longer-term pooled fund investments, meanwhile, have declined by approximately £562,000 from their initial cost, though the funds continue to generate dividend income of nearly 5 per cent and 3 per cent respectively.

findings.headline: The TFC green low carbon skills and economy line has spent its full £1,463k revised budget by 30 September 2026, with the forecast on budget.
findings.detail: This is a Towns Fund line within Regeneration. It is the only line in the paper where spend to date equals the full revised budget.
findings.matters: A Towns Fund line fully spent at the half-year point, against a number of Towns Fund lines with much lower spend to date, is a delivery signal a peer council running similar grant-funded programmes would compare against.
findings.figures: Original budget £782k; carry forward from 2025/26 £681k; revised budget £1,463k; spend to 30 September £1,463k; forecast outturn £1,463k; variance £0k.

findings.headline: Three housing acquisition lines show spend to 30 September against nil revised budgets: HAS_02 Bexhill Road Development £1,018k, SHAP £524k and HAS_01 LUP TA Acquisitions £334k, each forecast at nil.
findings.detail: The three lines carry zero original, carry-forward and revised budgets, and each has a forecast outturn of zero. The paper does not explain the spend against these lines.
findings.matters: Recorded capital spend without a budget line, or a budget moved elsewhere, is a control question a finance director would expect to see explained in the next report.
findings.figures: HAS_02 Bexhill Road Development: spend £1,018k against revised budget £0k. SHAP: spend £524k against revised budget £0k. HAS_01 LUP TA Acquisitions: spend £334k against revised budget £0k.
findings.quote: 71310 HAS_02 Bexhill Road Development Housing Susan Hanson 0 0 0 1,018 0 0

findings.headline: St Mary in the Castle pre-marketing works, which has a nil original and revised budget, is forecast at £617k with £19k spent to 30 September.
findings.detail: The forecast is shown as a variance of £617k against gross budget. The paper does not state how the forecast is to be funded.
findings.matters: Spend forecast against a nil budget is unfunded capital expenditure until a funding source is approved, which a finance director would need to resolve and a lender would want to see explained.
findings.figures: Revised budget £0k; spend to 30 September £19k; forecast outturn £617k; variance £617k.

findings.headline: Asset Management R&R is forecast at £827k against a revised budget of £1,780k, and Energy and Solar Panels at £638k against £1,138k, variances of £(953)k and £(500)k.
findings.detail: Both are Estates Services lines. Spend to 30 September is £78k on Asset Management R&R and £7k on Energy and Solar Panels.
findings.matters: Forecast underspends on property maintenance and energy schemes show where the council is not spending its approved capital, which a peer council or lender may compare against its own estates backlog.
findings.figures: Asset Management R&R: revised budget £1,780k, spend £78k, forecast £827k, variance £(953)k. Energy and Solar Panels: revised budget £1,138k, spend £7k, forecast £638k, variance £(500)k.

findings.headline: The unallocated Energy Initiatives (Generation) budget of £2,800k, including £1,900k carried forward from 2025/26, is forecast at £50k, a variance of £(2,750)k.
findings.detail: Spend to 30 September is £2k. This is the largest single variance in the paper and is recorded against an unallocated budget line rather than a named scheme.
findings.matters: A large unallocated capital budget forecast to be almost wholly unspent shows how an energy generation programme has been paused or not yet scoped, which bears on borrowing and on the council's energy investment plans.
findings.figures: Revised budget £2,800k; carry forward from 2025/26 £1,900k; spend to 30 September £2k; forecast outturn £50k; variance £(2,750)k.
